areas_of_law: Patent validity - specification sufficiency and misrepresentation
issues: Whether the patent is invalid for lack of demonstrated or soundly predicted utility, given the compound was never tested in humans before filing
Whether the doctrine of sound prediction was satisfied as of the filing/priority date based only on animal data

Whether inaccuracies between the patent's reported test data (species used, dosing/timing, toxicity figures) and the actual underlying lab records render the patent invalid for misrepresentation, insufficient disclosure, or lack of factual basis for the prediction

Whether statements in the patent regarding low toxicity, longer duration of action, and greater safety versus prior compounds constitute a 'promise of the patent' that, if unfulfilled, invalidates the claims

Whether a new invalidity argument (data inaccuracy) not pleaded in the original notice of allegation can be raised or considered given it was based on information obtained only through later disclosure/discovery
Whether the adequacy/sufficiency of the notice of allegation can be raised by the court on its own motion, and what standard applies
Whether the composition claim for treating senile dementia is separately vulnerable to inutility/overbreadth even if the compound claim survives
key_facts: Generic manufacturer filed an abbreviated new drug submission and served a notice of allegation (NOA) challenging validity of a listed compound patent
Brand company and foreign patent owner commenced prohibition/infringement-related proceeding to block regulatory approval pending patent expiry
Patent filed in the late 1980s, prosecuted based solely on animal (non-human) testing
Patent claims both the compound itself and a composition for treating senile dementia

Post-filing disclosure of lab notebooks revealed discrepancies: wrong rodent species reported for a brain tissue test, incorrect dosing/timing described in a learning-impairment study, and a toxicity figure that was extrapolated rather than actually administered
Client alleges patent text promises low toxicity, longer duration of action, and greater safety versus two comparator drugs
The data-accuracy invalidity argument was not raised in the original NOA because lab records were unavailable at that time
The judge raised the adequacy of the NOA sua sponte at the hearing
causes_of_action: Patent invalidity - lack of utility / no sound prediction
Patent invalidity - insufficiency of disclosure / inaccurate specification
Impeachment of patent validity in response to prohibition application
Procedural challenge to scope/adequacy of notice of allegation
search_terms: utility date of filing animal testing patent
amending notice of allegation new grounds
factual basis and line of reasoning sound prediction
listed patent compound composition claim senile dementia
court raising issue sua sponte notice of allegation adequacy
